title: Pinball Construction Set
tagline: Build your own pinball table, then play it.
summary: Bill Budge's Pinball Construction Set (Electronic Arts, 1983) lets you build a pinball machine on screen: take flippers, bumpers, kickers, targets, rollovers, gates and walls out of the box, put them on the table, bend the walls, paint them, wire up scores, bonuses and sounds, set gravity, speed, kick and elasticity, and play your table at once.
It was one of the first construction kits in a video game. Budge later published its source code under the MIT license.

This port is the Apple II program itself, translated routine by routine from Budge's 6502 listings and checked against them: the same hi-res screen with its colours, the same physics, scoring and sounds, the construction set with its magnifier, wiring kit and disk menu. The disk is your storage on the server; one to four players take turns at one keyboard, or play online, each at their own computer.
players: 1–4, taking turns (on one computer or online)

controls.action: The joystick: moves the hand (or the tool) on the screen
Button 0: pick up and drop parts, use a tool, choose in the menus
The plunger: pull it back, let go to shoot
One more player (up to 4); a button starts the game
Out of a test play or a game, back to the construction set
Type file names in the disk menu
Sound off and on in a game
